brief.subject: IRS can now take card payments directly, plus PTC changes
brief.headline: IRS Finalizes Rules to Accept Card Tax Payments Without Third-Party Processors
brief.dek: A final IRS rule clears the way for direct card payments, while proposed premium tax credit changes could hit self-insured freelancers.
brief.lede: The IRS has finalized rules letting it accept credit and debit card tax payments directly, cutting out third-party processors.

sections.heading: IRS cuts out card payment middlemen
bullets: Final regulations let the IRS take credit and debit card tax payments itself, no outside processor required.
The change implements Taxpayer First Act provisions, which could simplify how owners pay estimated and business taxes.
The rules also lift limits on the IRS paying fees under card-payment contracts, which could shape future processing costs.

sections.heading: Premium tax credit rules may change
bullets: Proposed regulations would revise who qualifies for the premium tax credit and how it is calculated.
Freelancers buying Exchange health coverage should watch closely, since repayment of excess advance credits is also covered.
These are proposals, not final rules, so current treatment still applies for now.

sections.heading: Adoption credit refunds now flowing
bullets: The IRS has begun refunding more than 50,000 taxpayers tied to the adoption tax credit carryforward.
The agency expects to wrap up the refunds by the end of the year, useful context for clients asking about status.

sections.heading: Scholarship credit opt-ins still pending
bullets: Sixteen governors, including Illinois' JB Pritzker, have not decided whether to join the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit program.
State participation determines whether taxpayers there can use the new credit, so client planning remains uncertain.
A researcher has projected how much scholarship money could reach public school students under the program.

brief.seo_description: IRS finalizes direct card tax payments, proposes premium tax credit changes, and starts adoption credit refunds to more than 50,000 taxpayers.

items.snippet: This document contains final regulations regarding the payment of tax by commercially acceptable means. items.title: Rule: Non-Applicability of Section 357(c) to Consolidated Groups
items.snippet: This document contains final regulations clarifying that, in the case of certain transfers between members of a consolidated group, a transferee's assumption of certain liabilities will not reduce the transferor's basis in the transferee's stock received in the transfer. These final regulations affect consolidated groups and their members.
